I've been watching over my elderly Grandmother for the past few weeks, because she absolutely refuses to go into a home, and it's extremely depressing to see how much a person can fall just because of old age. Mentally, my Grandma used to be a very smart, well-researched, and talented person, with a good opinion and knowledge on most things. One could have a reasonable discussion with her without a problem. Physically, she used to be able to cook, clean, and do regular things around the house. Now she can't even walk by herself most days, and refuses my help, of course.

Now when you have a conversation about anything with her, everything is either a badly recalled fact about the past that never happened, or an extremely left wing opinion on anything. For example, when I said (not trying to start a pointless discussion) that I don't blame Germany for not wanting to give Greece yet more money to pay off their debt, she said that the Germans love to do such heinous acts and it was just another Holocaust all over again, as if that was a regular occurring thing. I immediately ended the conversation. She also has a very, 1950's, idyllic view of everything. She thinks that New York City is a perfectly safe city for a 80 year old grandmother to walk around at 2AM and that Baltimore is made up of separate and distinct ethnic neighborhoods, and also a safe city. I spend a lot of time in both those cities, they are neither of those. When I use examples, she just quotes Racism or that she doesn't remember it that way. Whenever I bring up a reasonable source, like a news article or actual history that reasonably proves her wrong, she gets pissy and uppity about being wrong. For example, she thinks that all of the Bush family members have served in the military and have all gone to Military academies thanks to their father pulling strings to get in. She also thinks that if you have a family member that graduated from a military academy, their offspring could get in without a single problem. No need for sending an application, you're just let in. I did some research, and found that Jeb never served in the military, and GWB only went to a military school that goes along side High School. When I presented this information to her, she rejected it and said I didn't know what she knew about the presidents and their family. Everything is a conspiracy to her. I never try to be pushy about it, I'm just trying to be reasonable and stick to the facts. She has never done this in the past.

Last Thanksgiving, she had a terrible fall. Her lung was punctured by a few broken ribs and her hip was broken. The doctor told us if we weren't there to call 9/11 when we did, she would have drowned in her own blood and died. I bring this up, because despite this, she thinks she would be able to crawl to a phone and call 9/11 herself. I watched her fall, I saw her life nearly go from her body as she laid on that floor. No, she can't do that. She has also told me that she has fallen in the middle of the night, probably over all the old world crap she keeps around for no reason, and that she was fine then, so there is no concern in the event of another fall. There is a massive concern. She used to have Life Alert, but refused to keep it because "It doesn't work 12 feet outside my home." That's not what it is for. She also argues that it cost's $100 every time the button is pressed, and I know she doesn't fully know that because, she has never pressed the button when she had the service, she never fell when she had the service (to my knowledge), and that's the cost of the ambulance fees.

Also, she doesn't remember much of anything anymore. I took her to see Antman yesterday (Fantastic movie by the way), and she thought it was the first Superhero movie she had ever seen. It wasn't, we've been going to watch superhero movies since Iron Man came out in 07' She loves these movies, but she has forgotten all about them.

I've spent some time trying to think about how to solve this. Ideally, you could make the decision and go to a clinic yourself. It would be possible to fly to a country to do the same thing, but may be beyond an octogenarians means. I met someone who told me that they'd like a big bottle of whiskey and a bicycle, and they'd ride off into woods never to be seen again. That poses the problem of what happens to your body? There's not many places an old, sick person could go to that their body wouldn't be found fairly quickly, and I wouldn't want to impose that on anyone. Jumping from a building or a bridge presents the same problem, you're leaving a horrible mess for someone to find and clean up, and I don't want my final act to be... that. Hypothermia seems like the best option. Maybe climb a mountain, go off the beaten trail, and tuck yourself into some crag or crevice at the beginning of winter.

All in all, after much thought, it seems mostly impossible to do anything about it to me, unless as others have pointed out, we revise our laws on euthanasia.
